active_paradigms.idea: Replace fixed-width beam construction with admissible best-first branch-and-bound over transaction prefixes using heapq.heappush
active_paradigms.description: The current program uses exact simulator costs, which is its main strength, but it retains only at most eight prefixes at every depth. This aggressively discards prefixes whose partial cost is temporarily worse but whose later conflict orientations yield a much lower final makespan; relocate, swaps, reversals, and destroy/repair cannot reliably recover such lost orientations. Treat the exact cost of a prefix as a lower bound for every completion of that prefix, because adding transactions can only add operations and conflict constraints to the simulated workload. Maintain a min-heap of prefixes keyed by this lower bound, expand the currently most promising prefix, and retain a complete incumbent whenever a leaf is reached. Prune a prefix when its lower bound is at least the incumbent cost, and also deduplicate exact prefix tuples. Seed the incumbent with the current beam/LNS answer, so branch-and-bound immediately benefits from a strong upper bound rather than exploring blindly. If runtime must be bounded, stop after a deterministic expansion budget and return the best complete incumbent, not the best partial prefix. This directly optimizes the evaluator's exact makespan rather than using transaction length, write count, or a surrogate conflict score.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The primary scalar makespan, by avoiding beam-width errors and proving/pruning large portions of the permutation space using exact simulator-derived lower and upper bounds.
active_paradigms.cautions: Verify empirically that workload.get_opt_seq_cost(prefix) is monotone when transactions are appended before treating it as an admissible lower bound; if the simulator does not have this property, only use it for expansion priority, not pruning. Heap growth can be large on highly connected workloads, so impose a deterministic node budget and always preserve the incumbent. Do not prune merely because two prefixes contain the same set of transactions: their internal order can produce different timing frontiers and conflict directions.

active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.milp for a direct operation-level disjunctive scheduling model with transaction-rank variables
active_paradigms.description: The current local search searches only transaction permutations and evaluates each candidate exactly, but it has no global mechanism to coordinate many mutually interacting conflict choices. Formulate one integer rank variable per transaction and one continuous start/completion-time variable per operation, plus a makespan variable. Preserve each transaction's internal operation order through precedence constraints. For every pair of operations from different transactions that conflict on the same key, introduce a binary orientation variable and big-M precedence constraints, so either operation A precedes B or B precedes A. Link each orientation to the transaction ranks so all conflicts between a transaction pair use the same globally serializable order, and add rank-all-different constraints using binary pairwise order variables or an assignment-style rank encoding. Minimize the makespan variable directly with scipy.optimize.milp, then sort transaction IDs by the solved rank and validate the resulting permutation through workload.get_opt_seq_cost. This is fundamentally stronger than using a conflict-count proxy: all operation durations, intra-transaction chains, and the actual maximum completion time are present in the objective. It is particularly valuable for medium-sized dense conflict components, where a local optimum can require several simultaneous transaction-order changes to escape.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The exact makespan objective globally, especially interacting read-write/write-write conflict orientations that cannot be fixed by one relocation, swap, or greedy reinsertion.
active_paradigms.cautions: Use a safe finite big-M derived from the total number of operations or another valid upper bound on makespan, and keep time variables nonnegative. Do not create binaries for nonconflicting operation pairs. MILP can become large for every operation-pair conflict, so restrict it to manageable connected components or use a strict solver time limit and use the incumbent schedule if the solver returns only a feasible solution. Always re-evaluate the extracted transaction permutation with the simulator because tie handling in ranks must still produce a valid unique order.

active_paradigms.idea: Exploit exact independence by finding transaction conflict components with scipy.sparse.csgraph.connected_components
active_paradigms.description: The present program spends its beam and neighborhood-search budget over all transactions even when some groups never access a conflicting item. Build an undirected transaction conflict graph, adding an edge whenever two transactions have a read-write or write-write conflict on any key, then call scipy.sparse.csgraph.connected_components on its sparse adjacency matrix. Transactions in distinct connected components have no cross-component conflict edge, so their operation timing and their relative transaction positions cannot affect one another. Consequently, optimize each nontrivial component independently with the exact-cost search strategy, and concatenate component permutations in a deterministic order; the simulator can overlap independent components, so their overall contribution is governed by their independent timing rather than by an artificial cross-component ordering. Singleton transactions should be included without search. This decomposition makes exact best-first search or the operation-level MILP viable on components that would be intractable when combined, while preserving global optimality with respect to cross-component ordering because no such conflicts exist. It also identifies the true hard core: a giant component merits the expensive search, whereas isolated components should not consume beam slots or LNS attempts.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary makespan and search budget allocation, by removing conflict-independent transactions from the combinatorial ordering problem and concentrating exact optimization on connected conflict components.
active_paradigms.cautions: Edges must include write-write and read-write conflicts but exclude read-read pairs. Only decompose on true transaction conflict independence; shared keys with reads only must not create edges, while any write on either side must. Confirm that the simulator has no hidden global resource, commit-order, or transaction-start restriction beyond item conflicts; if it does, component concatenation may not be exact. Preserve all transaction IDs exactly once when assembling the final global sequence and recheck its simulator cost.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use exact permutation enumeration for small transaction counts with itertools.permutations
tried_paradigms.description: The current program is a deterministic beam search over prefixes, followed by relocation, swap, and interval-reversal descent. Its key strength is that every comparison uses workload.get_opt_seq_cost rather than a surrogate based only on lengths or write counts. However, its beam discards prefixes solely on partial-prefix cost, even though a prefix that is temporarily expensive can produce a substantially better final dependency orientation; its local neighborhoods also cannot cross deep permutation valleys. When n is small enough that n! simulator calls fit the evaluation budget, replace heuristic construction entirely with itertools.permutations(range(n)) and score every complete permutation using get_opt_seq_cost. Retain the minimum cost and use lexicographic order as a deterministic tie-breaker. This directly optimizes exactly the same scalar the simulator and evaluator use, so it is globally optimal rather than merely locally optimal. A practical guarded implementation can enumerate exactly only below a conservative cutoff and use the incumbent beam method above that cutoff, but the exact branch should be preferred whenever workloads have roughly 8–9 transactions or fewer. This is fundamentally different from trying to tune the current beam width or add another local move.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The actual makespan returned by workload.get_opt_seq_cost; exact enumeration removes all prefix-ranking and local-optimum errors for feasible workload sizes.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Do not evaluate partial permutations as though they were comparable to final schedules in the exact path. Cache complete tuple costs only if repeated evaluations can arise, and choose the factorial cutoff from the evaluator timeout and observed get_opt_seq_cost latency. Preserve the required return shape of (best_cost, best_sequence).

tried_paradigms.idea: Use simulator-guided randomized iterated local search with random.Random.shuffle perturbations
tried_paradigms.description: The existing search is deterministic: all beam branches are ranked by the same partial-cost rule, and only the best few complete finalists receive improvement. Consequently it can repeatedly converge to the same basin, particularly when many initial single-transaction costs tie. Use a dedicated seeded random.Random instance to generate diverse full permutation starts and, after a local optimum is reached, perturb it by shuffling a selected block or a selected set of transaction positions before applying the same simulator-scored relocation and exchange descent. Accept strictly improving global incumbents, but also continue from perturbed local optima rather than restarting only from greedy prefixes. This targets the principal blind spot of the present code: a beneficial schedule may require several individually non-improving order changes before its conflict directions become favorable. Allocate the number of perturbation/restart attempts from num_seqs, so the caller’s search-budget parameter controls diversity rather than merely limiting beam width. Score every candidate with get_opt_seq_cost, never with operation counts or conflict counts, because the simulator captures timing and overlap effects that a static heuristic misses. A fixed seed makes the result reproducible for an evaluator while still exploring basins that the current deterministic beam cannot reach.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Lower makespan through escape from relocation/swap/reversal local minima and broader coverage of full-order permutation space.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Use a local Random instance with a fixed deterministic seed; do not use unseeded global randomness, which can add evaluator variance. Bound the number of full simulator calls carefully, retain the globally best schedule even when exploring worse perturbed states, and avoid perturbing only adjacent items because that is too similar to the current swap neighborhood.

tried_paradigms.idea: Generate a conflict-structure spectral order using numpy.linalg.eigh
tried_paradigms.description: Build an undirected weighted transaction-conflict matrix directly from the workload operations: for each pair of transactions and each common key, add weight only when at least one access is a write, with weight proportional to the number of conflicting access pairs. Form its graph Laplacian and call numpy.linalg.eigh on that symmetric matrix. Sort transaction indices by the Fiedler-vector coordinate to obtain a global spectral ordering candidate, and evaluate that complete order with get_opt_seq_cost. Unlike the current beam, this considers all transactions and their conflict topology simultaneously before committing to early prefix choices. The rationale is that transactions with strongly coupled conflict patterns are positioned coherently, avoiding arbitrary early orientations caused by ties in one-transaction prefix cost; disconnected components can be deterministically concatenated because they have no cross-conflict contribution. Evaluate both the Fiedler order and its reverse, because an undirected Laplacian has no preferred direction whereas read/write sequence direction changes the simulator’s makespan. This is a cheap, structurally distinct seed that can outperform greedy prefix selection on dense clustered conflict graphs, and it can also be compared directly against the current beam result using the exact simulator objective.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Makespan lost by myopic prefix construction, especially on workloads whose conflict graph has clusters or near-disconnected components that should be ordered as coherent groups.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Extract operation/key information using the actual Workload representation rather than assuming a nonexistent public field; if only the input mapping is accessible, parse it consistently with Workload. Read-read overlaps must have zero edge weight. Handle all-zero or disconnected Laplacians deterministically, and do not assume the spectral score itself predicts makespan: get_opt_seq_cost must select the final winner.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace fixed-width beam search with admissible best-first branch-and-bound over transaction prefixes using heapq
tried_paradigms.description: The current program evaluates true simulator costs for prefixes, which is a major strength, but then irrevocably discards all but at most eight prefixes and locally improves only four completed orders. Treat each prefix as a search-tree node and store it in a priority queue ordered by an admissible lower bound: at minimum, the simulator makespan of that prefix, since adding transactions cannot remove already required work. Obtain a feasible incumbent early from the current beam/greedy construction, then prune every prefix whose lower bound is already no better than that incumbent. Expand the most promising surviving prefix by appending each unplaced transaction, always scoring children through workload.get_opt_seq_cost rather than a surrogate. Add a conflict-aware secondary key, such as the remaining transaction's number of read/write conflicts with already placed transactions, only for tie-breaking; simulator cost remains the decision criterion. Use num_seqs as an expansion/evaluation budget so the search is anytime: it returns the incumbent if the budget expires, but can prove or approach optimality on smaller instances. Memoize full prefix costs and retain several distinct prefixes even when they have equal cost, because their future conflict orientations differ. This directly addresses the principal beam weakness while preserving what makes the existing solution effective: optimization against the exact evaluator-facing cost function.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The sole evaluator-relevant quantity is the makespan returned by workload.get_opt_seq_cost for the final permutation. The priority and pruning bound should therefore be based on that exact makespan, not transaction length, write count, or a graph proxy.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The visible evaluator wrapper only serializes calls and delegates to hidden evaluator.py, so do not assume any extra score component beyond the simulator result. The monotonic-prefix lower-bound argument must be verified against the simulator; if a partial prefix can report a cost larger than a later complete prefix, use the prefix value only as priority and disable cost-based pruning. Keep a hard evaluation/node budget, since factorial expansion is otherwise infeasible for large workloads.

tried_paradigms.idea: Solve the operation-level disjunctive scheduling formulation directly as a mixed-integer linear program with scipy.optimize.milp
tried_paradigms.description: Instead of searching permutations indirectly, formulate the schedule that the simulator is effectively evaluating. Create a start-time variable for every read/write operation and add unit-duration chain constraints for consecutive operations within each transaction. For every pair of operations from different transactions that conflict on a key, introduce a binary orientation variable deciding which operation precedes the other, with big-M precedence constraints in the chosen direction. Couple all conflict orientations between a transaction pair to a single binary transaction-order variable when the simulator requires one global order per transaction pair, and introduce integer rank variables plus standard rank/order constraints to eliminate cyclic transaction orders. Add a makespan variable constrained to be at least every operation completion time and minimize it with scipy.optimize.milp using integrality for orientation and rank variables. Convert the resulting transaction ranks into the required sequence, then call get_opt_seq_cost once to validate the candidate and return that exact cost rather than trusting the MILP objective. This differs fundamentally from the current beam-plus-local-search method: it considers all pairwise conflict directions jointly, so it can cross barriers requiring many simultaneous relocations or reversals. It is especially promising when transaction counts are modest but operations and repeated conflicts make local permutation neighborhoods deceptive.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Minimize the operation-level Cmax/makespan, with the final ordering selected by the exact workload.get_opt_seq_cost result. The MILP should model only read-write and write-write conflicts; read-read pairs must not introduce unnecessary serialization.
tried_paradigms.cautions: This is correct only after matching the simulator semantics precisely, including operation durations, whether a conflict is enforced by transaction order or individual operation order, and any lock-release behavior. A naive per-operation orientation model may produce a schedule that cannot be represented by the single returned transaction permutation, so enforce global transaction-order consistency if required. Choose M from a safe upper bound such as the total number of operations, set a practical time_limit option, and fall back to the best incumbent sequence if scipy reports no feasible integer solution.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use randomized large-neighborhood destroy-and-greedy-repair restarts driven entirely by exact simulator insertion costs
tried_paradigms.description: The current descent examines relocations, swaps, and interval reversals only around a small set of deterministic beam finalists, so it cannot leave a basin when every one-transaction move is temporarily harmful. Start from the best current permutation, randomly remove a block of several transactions, and rebuild the partial order by inserting each removed transaction at every possible position while selecting the insertion with minimum workload.get_opt_seq_cost. Bias removal toward transactions participating in many actual read-write/write-write conflicts with the rest of the order, because changing those positions has the greatest chance to alter the critical path. Perform many independent destroy-and-repair attempts, retaining the globally best schedule, and vary removal size from small perturbations to a substantial fraction of transactions. For each repair, randomize the order in which removed transactions are reinserted; this explores different conflict orientations even when their initial insertion scores tie. Optionally accept a non-improving repaired schedule only as the seed for a later restart, while never replacing the globally reported best result. Every accept/reject comparison and every insertion choice uses the simulator cost, avoiding the unsupported length/write-count heuristics warned against in the task. This gives a much larger effective neighborhood than the current pair swaps and reversals without requiring a full factorial search.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Optimize final simulator makespan across diversified restarts; the conflict count is only used to choose which transactions to perturb, never as a substitute objective.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Fix a local random.Random seed or derive it deterministically from workload contents if evaluator reproducibility matters; hidden scoring may penalize unstable outcomes. Bound the number of candidate insertion evaluations and restarts by num_seqs or a fixed budget, since repair cost grows with removal size and transaction count. Always preserve a valid complete permutation and return workload.get_opt_seq_cost(best_sequence), not a stale cached or surrogate value.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace shallow relocate/swap search with deterministic critical-disruption block ejection chains
tried_paradigms.description: The current program is simulator-guided, which is its principal strength: every accepted move is evaluated by the true makespan rather than a conflict-count proxy. However, it only reaches local optima under one-item relocation, swap, reversal, and a greedy repair; a bad orientation often requires moving several transactions together before any intermediate one-item move improves. Starting from the incumbent, evaluate removal of each contiguous block of length 2 through a small bound such as 5, then reinsert that block in every destination gap and in both internal orientations. Rank candidate source blocks by their best exact cost decrease, accept the best improving ejection-chain move, and repeat until no block move improves. For a stronger neighborhood, after removing a block, allow one displaced transaction at its destination to be inserted into the original block gap; this changes several conflict directions in one exact move without random perturbation. Restrict full enumeration to blocks touching positions whose removal causes the largest exact cost change, keeping runtime bounded. Unlike the prior failed randomized-shuffle ILS, this is deterministic, systematically searches a strictly larger neighborhood, and never relies on random repair luck. Return only a complete permutation and its exact `get_opt_seq_cost` value, so it preserves evaluator validity.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The primary scalar makespan directly, especially schedules trapped in a one-transaction relocate/swap local optimum where a coordinated reversal or displacement is required to shorten the critical conflict chain.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Do not score a block by a conflict-count proxy; compare complete permutations with the simulator. Cache tuple permutations, deduplicate candidates, and cap block length/candidate count because each ejection-chain round is quadratic to cubic in transaction count. Accept only strict improvements, with deterministic lexicographic tie-breaking, so the result is reproducible and cannot regress relative to the current incumbent.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use admissible best-first branch-and-bound over transaction prefixes instead of using prefix cost only as beam ranking
tried_paradigms.description: The current beam retains only 2–8 prefixes with the lowest cost on the transactions seen so far. That prefix score is useful, but it is not a safe indication of which prefix will yield the best complete order: a temporarily expensive prefix can orient high-impact conflicts correctly and become globally best. Treat `get_opt_seq_cost(prefix)` as an admissible lower bound whenever adding transactions cannot remove operations or constraints from the already scheduled prefix, which is the natural monotonicity property of this simulator. Seed an incumbent with the current beam/LNS result, then use a priority queue of partial prefixes ordered by a lower bound rather than permanently discarding all but the beam width. Strengthen that bound by taking the maximum of the prefix makespan and a remaining-work lower bound based on each unscheduled transaction's internal operation-chain length; this is still admissible because every remaining transaction must execute its own chain. Expand a prefix only if its bound is below the incumbent, and branch first on the remaining transaction whose append-to-prefix exact cost is most discriminating, so good incumbents appear early and pruning increases. Memoize states by `(frozenset(used), last few order-sensitive transactions)` only when the simulator semantics make that equivalence sound; otherwise memoize exact prefixes only. With a fixed node/time budget, return the best incumbent, while on small and medium instances this can certify an optimum rather than merely improving a local optimum.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Direct makespan minimization and, where the workload size permits, global optimality; it specifically corrects the current beam search's irreversible pruning error.
tried_paradigms.cautions: First verify monotonicity empirically on a few prefixes: if the simulator's prefix call has semantics other than scheduling only those transactions, do not use it as a pruning lower bound. Never prune on a heuristic estimate that can exceed the achievable completion cost. Retain a valid incumbent at all times so a node-budget cutoff safely returns a schedule. This is fundamentally different from the failed full permutation enumeration because it explores only prefixes that can still beat an exact incumbent.

tried_paradigms.idea: Formulate the global transaction order and operation timing as a direct mixed-integer linear program
tried_paradigms.description: Build an exact disjunctive scheduling model rather than searching permutations through local moves. Create a start-time variable for every operation, impose unit-duration intra-transaction precedence constraints, and create one binary orientation variable for each pair of operations from different transactions that conflict on the same item with at least one write. Couple every such orientation to a single transaction-pair ordering binary, so all conflicts between the same two transactions respect one global sequence direction. Add antisymmetry and transitivity/order-position constraints for transaction-pair binaries, use standard big-M precedence inequalities for conflicting operations, and minimize a makespan variable constrained to finish after every operation. `scipy.optimize.milp` then solves the actual global ordering problem rather than a surrogate such as transaction length or graph degree. Extract transaction ranks from the integral order variables, sort by rank, and validate that exact simulator cost; if the simulator cost differs because of an unmodeled semantic detail, use the MILP schedule only when validation improves the incumbent. Sparse constraint construction is important because the model size should scale with actual conflicting operation pairs, not all operation pairs. This route is qualitatively different from random search, spectral ordering, and brute-force permutations: it can reason simultaneously about all conflict directions and the critical path.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The exact makespan objective globally, with particular benefit on dense conflict workloads where independent greedy insertion makes mutually inconsistent ordering decisions.
tried_paradigms.cautions: This is viable only if operation durations and `get_opt_seq_cost` semantics can be reproduced from the available workload representation; confirm on small instances before trusting it. Set a finite MILP time limit and request the best incumbent solution, since dense workloads can have many binary variables. Choose a safe big-M no smaller than the total number of operations, enforce integrality when extracting ranks, and use deterministic tie-breaking for equal ranks. Do not replace exact simulator validation with the MILP objective if the simulator has additional constraints.
